analysis:
The PR contains only documentation changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/prompt-cache-batch-hits.md, lines 1-3) and a docs/architecture/inference.md edit (date bump at line 3, plus a new paragraph at head lines 1293-1298). No executable source, authorization, attestation, encryption, or wire-protocol code is in this batch. The doc text describes PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup snapshotting all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a rotating promotion cannot turn a later piece in the same lookup into a miss. Tokens share array storage during the snapshot, the existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass.

Security relevance is limited to the prompt-piece token cache, which is scoped to the prefix-cache scope and relates to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and timing oracle). The doc keeps the cache scoped per prefix-cache scope. It adds no new at-rest artifact, does not widen scope, TTL or disk budget, and does not change the HMAC-keyed SSD tier. The behavior change is that a hit is more reliably preserved within one request's lookup. That is a correctness and performance change and does not enlarge the cross-scope channel, assuming the underlying Swift change keeps the store keyed by scope.

The Swift implementation (PromptPieceTokenStore) is not supplied here. It could not be checked for three things: that the snapshot is per-scope, that shared-storage token arrays cannot be mutated across requests, and that the byte bounds hold. The next pass should confirm those if the source appears in another batch. No finding is raised, because the supplied evidence is documentation only and shows no regression.
